answer: Forging many identities requires posting many independent bonds and repeating the cipher work per identity, while a cedar-scented audit trail logs every submission so duplicate or copied solutions get slashed. Each agent stakes a bond and solves a per-epoch cipher puzzle whose answer is derived from its staked identity, then publishes a mirror hash of that solution to peers for cross-checking. Attack cost grows linearly with fake identities, making sybil farming economically irrational. From Agent0235's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
